_comment: Fragment 44 — D-91: Lane B made startable. S0 single-laned, entry point written, G27 closed, stale tails struck. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-91 — Lane B Made Startable
nodes.description: Applies the four gaps D-90 surfaced and left drafted: S0's deliverables no longer mix lanes, Lane B has an entry point, G27's draft location is decided, and the dead needs_update instruction is struck from the two tails that still carried it.
nodes.rationale: D-90 built the channel Lane B reports through. None of it made Lane B able to start. These four would each have bitten on its first day, and the first three are one dependency chain rather than four independent fixes.

nodes.label: S0 Single-Laned: Lane A Provisions the Governance Content
nodes.description: S0 listed two docs files, DECISION_LOG and CONFIG_LOG, alongside Lane B code. Lane B's first sprint therefore required a lane crossing that the commit hook installed one commit earlier would block. Lane A now owns both logs content included and wrote them ahead of the sprint.
nodes.rationale: A lane cannot own a file whose content it is instructed not to understand. A log row is a citation into the governing set plus an Open Decision dependency, which is governance, and under D-86 Lane B is explicitly not expected to read the register. Ownership resolves this, not permission.

nodes.label: The Gate and the Sprint Plan Contradicted Each Other Undetected
nodes.description: lane-boundary classifies commits, not plans. A sprint plan is not a commit until someone executes it, so a plan that mandates a crossing passes every check until Lane B's first git commit, with the work already done.
nodes.rationale: A detection control bounded to one representation of the work cannot see the same defect in another. The same shape as source-sweep being the inverse of tier-sweep: the instrument looked in one direction only.

nodes.label: G27 Closed — a Location Asserted in Passing, Never Decided
nodes.description: D-68's rationale stated that G27 holds the 0002 draft at docs/v1/drafts/. The §5.1 row said Open, the inventory said Location decision, and the directory did not exist. D-91 adopts that path rather than inventing a second one, and creates the directory. The draft file stays unwritten because G64 and Q11 still gate it.
nodes.rationale: The register answered the question inside a paragraph about something else and never recorded the answer as an answer. This is D-90's defect in a second instance: D-75 required a handoff and named no place, D-17 required a hold and its place was named only in passing. Both were found by trying to use the thing.

nodes.label: DECISION_LOG Cites the Register, Never Restates It
nodes.description: The ratification ledger records ratification events for the decisions that gate a config value. It is deliberately not a second decision register. Its §3 table is empty, and the emptiness is the finding: OD1 through OD3 have gated this build since the Charter and none has been ratified.
nodes.rationale: A DECISION_LOG that paraphrased the register would be summary outliving source by construction. Two things live here that the register deliberately does not carry: Chief Editor ratification against build evidence, and unratified A-item values running live in Phase 0.

nodes.label: G73 — a Per-Agent Correction Reaches One Agent
nodes.description: shared-core-hash compares only the region between the markers. Tails are excluded by design because they differ per agent. D-87 struck the dead needs_update instruction from CLAUDE.md's tail and the other two files carried it for four days with every check green.
nodes.rationale: G53 named the same shape for the shared region and was closed by hashing it. That instrument does not transfer: a control that fires on every intended difference is worse than none. Recorded as an open residual with no control proposed, so the next per-agent correction is known to need manual propagation.

nodes.label: C-17 — the Config Log and the Code Are Uncoupled
nodes.description: Lane A owns every CONFIG_LOG row and Lane B owns build-config.ts. Nothing pairs them, so a variable can be added to one and missed in the other with all checks green. The fix is a bidirectional C-14 check, deliberately not built until build-config.ts exists.
nodes.rationale: Built now, the check would pass on every run without ever reading a variable. The split ownership D-91 introduces is exactly what makes this drift silent rather than obvious to one author, so the condition is opened in the same pass that creates the risk.
